comparator.sourceNotes: The ordinary Religious Studies bachelor closes 60+60+60. Its compulsory 24-EC first-year restricted package is instantiated as the first complete current option: Introduction to Anthropology (12 EC) plus Current Debates 1: Connecting Worlds (12 EC). This is a bounded first-year package, not an invented graduation track. The separately listed shortened 120-EC route is excluded. The thesis project and thesis retain their completion gates; 30 EC of genuine profiling stays generic. Diagnostic and tutoring formation are zero-credit. Current evidence supports Dutch and English instruction.

exception.reason: Three independently organised directions were tested. Comparative religion, traditions, sacred texts and belief/practice fails because UCR offers no comparative-religion survey, sustained teaching of major traditions, sacred-text interpretation or religious-studies theory. Religion in society, identity, public life and conflict has genuine sociology, politics, law and qualitative methods, but no sociology or anthropology of religion, religion-and-politics sequence or religion-specific field research. Lived religion, spirituality, culture and contemporary change has isolated encounters with myth, religiously inflected literature, material culture, art and Buddhist thought, but no coherent study of ritual, spirituality, secularisation, pluralism or religion in media and popular culture. In every direction, extending adjacent disciplines to 23 non-PPD courses would change the object of study away from religion. The gap is academic substance rather than professional qualification, so no complete UCR response is claimed.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and Fall-2026-start availability. MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works discusses organised religion within a broad literary survey, and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature compares myths as literary traditions. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology and MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage encounter religious material culture, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy includes ancient Greek religion, GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind briefly considers Buddhist thought, and GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law mentions religious constitutions and rights. GOSSOCI111/212/214/311, GOSPOLI111/112/212/313, GOSPHIL111/212 and GOSLAWJ111 provide adjacent social, political, ethical and methodological study. None teaches comparative religion, Christianity, Judaism, Islam and Buddhism as traditions, sacred-text methods, ritual, lived religion, secularisation, religious pluralism, sociology or anthropology of religion, or religion-specific research. These isolated encounters cannot anchor a coherent 24-course Religious Studies response.

candidateAssessment.concept: Comparative religion, traditions, sacred texts and belief/practice
candidateAssessment.assessment: Broad philosophy, literature, myth and cultural-history courses encounter selected religious ideas or materials, but UCR has no comparative-religion survey, sustained study of major traditions, sacred-text interpretation, religious-studies historiography or religion-specific independent research. The direction lacks both its object and disciplinary methods.

candidateAssessment.concept: Religion in society, identity, public life and conflict
candidateAssessment.assessment: Sociology, politics, law, conflict studies and qualitative research provide relevant frameworks for public life and identity. Their documented content does not teach sociology or anthropology of religion, religion and politics, religious communities, pluralism or religion-specific qualitative fieldwork, so a full programme would become generic social science.

candidateAssessment.concept: Lived religion, spirituality, culture and contemporary change
candidateAssessment.assessment: Literature, myth, art, archaeology, media and philosophy offer isolated religiously inflected examples. They do not form a sequence in lived religion, ritual, spirituality, secularisation, religious art, digital religion or religion in popular culture. Expanding those adjacent courses would produce cultural studies without religion as a sustained object.
